overview: Event Venue Capacity and Flow Planning addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in hospitality and tourism operations. The first proof of value uses registration, entrance sensors and event layouts. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is queue time at venue entry, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: registration, entrance sensors and event layouts; define queue time at venue entry and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Hotel GM / Hospitality Revenue Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for queue time at venue entry
